assistant_text:
Challenge the assumed customer response to a £59 price—especially whether the feature release offsets price resistance.

- The model assumes higher price raises MRR, while price resistance affects both new subscribers and churn; it does not contain evidence for the size of those effects.
- This is the key fragility: changing the Pro-price-to-MRR relationship can alter the comparison.
- Also challenge the Olumi estimates of **300** active Pro subscribers, **20/month** new Pro subscribers, **3% monthly churn**, and a **65/100** feature-value score.

If only one: test likely conversion, upgrade and churn changes at £59 versus £49.
